result:
T5 is done, and its verify command exits 0 (it prints `gate T5 ok`).

I added `internal/metrics/time.go` and `internal/metrics/time_test.go`. Nothing else was touched, and I did not edit `state.json` or commit.

- **`Aggregate(m, delivered)`**:
  - Time: agent time is work plus review, plan time is kept apart, and gate time is the sum of recorded gate durations. Wall time runs from the plan commit to the last run commit.
  - Rates: code lines per minute, and code plus test, both on agent time.
  - Cost: sums of the unrounded session costs per phase and in total, plus cost per 1,000 delivered code lines.
  - Tokens: input, output, cache read and cache creation, with the cache-hit ratio.
  - Models and effort: sorted, comma-joined lists per phase.
- **`CountTasks`**: planned, done and blocked come from the plan at the last run commit. A task is first-pass only if it has iterations and every one ended `done`, so a blocked-then-done task is not first-pass. It also returns the brief's `<n> to <m> tasks` estimate and iterations per closed task.
- **`MissingRecords`**: reports `<task> <phase> (iteration <i>)` for any iteration with no work session record. It does the same for `done`, `review_fail` and `rejected` iterations with no review session record.

Unknowns come back as nil rather than zero: gate time for the shell loop, wall time when there is no run commit, and any rate or ratio with a zero denominator.

Missing records are only reported. Whatever session records do exist for that iteration are still summed, and nothing is estimated in their place.

The tests are `TestTimeCost…`, `TestTasks…` and `TestMissingRecords…`, using temporary-directory fixtures. The worked example reproduces agent 160000 ms, plan 120000 ms, wall 600000 ms, $2.10, $140 per 1,000 code lines and first-pass 1/2. The plan session sits in its own folder, and one test covers blocked-then-done.

The proposal is at `.loop/tmp/proposal.json`.
